page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs spanning 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives. Memory capacity is configured at 384 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. High-speed local ephemeral capacity is provided via a bundled 5,669 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier parallel compute and data delivery capability. The instance records a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,967 and a PassMark CPU score of 86,698.13, placing it within the top 10% of evaluated hardware. Memory throughput remains robust, delivering 257.11 GB/sec on large read blocks and uncached writes reaching 107.03 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reaches 116.39 GB/sec. In memory-bound and transactional workloads, the D96ds_v6 achieves 107.53 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database operations scaling.

The qualitative hardware profile balances high CPU density, memory capacity, and expansive local NVMe storage without requiring dedicated memory-optimized hardware tiers. However, single-core execution sits in the middle 50% on stress-ng tests, indicating that its performance efficiency is heavily reliant on thread-level parallelism and instruction extensions like AMX and AVX-512 rather than raw per-thread frequency.

Microsoft Azure D96ds_v6 is well aligned for large-scale enterprise workloads that demand rapid local temporary storage alongside massive parallel processing. Prime use cases include relational and NoSQL database hosting, high-throughput web serving, parallel build and compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inferencing.

Benchmark results place its multi-core performance in the top 10%, achieving 21,967 points in Geekbench multi-core, 86,698.13 in PassMark CPU, and 116.39 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Redis performance scales to 107.53 million operations per second, supported by fast memory bandwidth and hardware extensions like AVX-512 and AMX. While single-threaded processing is moderate, the balance of high core counts, substantial memory, and rapid local NVMe storage delivers strong resource efficiency for databases, CI/CD compilation, and enterprise web services.
